title: read scans every element; write marks the end of what you keep
caption: The example keeps only the non-negative readings of a sensor log, in place. The shaded window is the kept prefix nums[0 .. write-1].

frames.text: Start: read = write = 0. Nothing has been kept yet, so the kept prefix is empty.
4 ≥ 0 was kept (nums[0] = 4, write = 1), and now read = 1. −1 is negative, so it's skipped and write stays at 1, the slot for the next kept value.
read = 2: 7 is kept. nums[1] = 7 and write = 2. read is never behind write, so you never overwrite a value you still have to read.
read = 3 and 4 are skipped (−3, −2). Then at read = 5, 5 is kept: nums[2] = 5 and write = 3.
read has run off the end. The answer is the prefix nums[0..2] = [4, 7, 5], and the new length is write = 3. Whatever sits after write doesn't matter.
